I\'m Lorenzo Langstroth. This operation is yours. We start with 45,000 beecoins and a calendar that moves day by day. The bees work while you\'re away.
Up top are your money and your level. Leveling up opens new climates. Selling honey, installing apiaries and buying hives grant experience.
The day\'s weather decides how much nectar there is. A bad day produces less. The colony keeps going.
Home is the summary. Apiaries are your farms. The map is where you install. The market is where honey goes out. From Home you can also pick a market and sell.
The first step is an apiary. Open the map.
Green fill is available. Red is locked: that climate needs a higher level. Border color is the climate, and the legend below tells you which is which. Your plot is painted violet.
Tap a point inside a green hexagon where you want to install your first apiary.
Wild flora is already on the plot. Below you see slots, climate and saturation: roomy leaves margin, saturated gives no more. The price is the apiary payment. Enter the name and confirm.
Tap the apiary image on the map to enter.
Buy the first hive and place it in the apiary.
Choose the flower the bees will take nectar from. Tapping it opens a chart: the honey flows and whether that flower is available through the year. Pick one that has a flow now.
Tap the hive in the apiary.
Up top you see honey, the queen and varroa. The queen drives brood. If varroa rises, treat it. Feeding lowers consumption on weak days.

This is Harvest. 3 kg always stay inside: that reserve is the colony's food.
Feed cuts the bees' own honey use by 50% while it lasts.
Treat varroa holds the mite for 7 days. You buy the treatment in the shop.
Replace queen swaps the current one: the brood depends on her.
Transhumance takes the hive to another apiary by truck. The price depends on the distance.
Without a honey house there is no shipment, and the harvest goes toward it. Install it on your violet hex: tap the plot and choose honey house. Honey is stored there and the truck leaves from there.
I\'ll advance one day so you see the cycle. In a normal game the day runs on its own.
On Home, tap Harvest. Honey goes to the honey house; then tap Sell and choose the nearest market or whichever suits you.
Open the market for more detail. From Home you can also pick a market and sell.

Each type has its price and demand. The shipment leaves the honey house for the provincial market once the truck has picked up the honey. Orders have specific deliveries. Contracts send hives to someone else\'s farm and you get paid for the service.
That\'s the craft: apiary, hive, day, harvest, honey house and market. When you do something new, I\'ll be back. You can replay this chapter from the dashboard menu.
Feeding covers one day or seven. On those days the colony consumes less honey.
Antivarroa treatment lasts 7 days. If you let it rise, the colony collapses.
A new queen changes brood quality. The 3 kg reserve is not touched when harvesting.

The reward is the pay if you meet the minimum. Any honey they collect is still yours.

The truck carries honey and, depending on its level, hives. Slots come from the honey house level.

The ship moves honey between regions. It does not move hives. The truck takes the load from honey house to port, and the ship continues by sea.
The ship\'s route shows on the map, just like the truck on the road.

From now on, the honey you harvest goes to the honey house. That\'s where it is extracted and packed. Without a honey house you can\'t harvest.
Each honey house stores honey and processes it. It comes with the reception room, and whatever you pack stays right here.
Buy the uncapper, the extractor, the maturing tank and the packing machine. That\'s 10,500 B. If one is missing, batches stop there.
Each batch goes through reception, uncapping, extraction, maturing and packing. Each machine works one batch at a time and the rest wait in line. Time keeps running even with the app closed.
Now you can harvest. The truck takes the supers to the honey house. When the first batch arrives, I\'ll show you how to pack it.
Your first batch is here. You can see which machine it\'s in and how long it has left.
Tap Choose container. The drum goes to the honey house and sells in bulk. Jars pay much better, and the smaller the jar, the more per kilo, but they take longer to pack.
Jars stay in the honey house. Sell them at the market or take them to orders that ask for jars. Wax comes from uncapping and sells at 9 B/kg.
Each machine level shortens its time and fits more honey per batch. The maturing tank adds one tank per level.
